clue.text: Refuse admission to bishop in close

indicators.note: in tells us the bishop's letter goes inside the word for close

parts.note: a close friend is a dear one, so close gives DEAR
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A bishop is turned away from the cathedral close.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close' looks like a noun (a cathedral close) but works as an adjective meaning intimate, DEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: To bar someone from a place is to keep them out, a formal synonym for refusing entry.

clue.text: Go away, mad with one's male, splitting up

parts.note: to depart is to go away
mental is informal for mad
one's is read as I'S, the Roman numeral one plus s

explanation.surface: A partner leaves, furious with a man, as the couple breaks up.
explanation.definitionFit: Departmentalism is the dividing of an organisation into separate departments, a breaking up into sections.

clue.text: Having succeeded in craft, exhibit

indicators.note: in places the letter for succeeded inside the word for craft

parts.note: a boat is a craft, a vessel
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, used in family trees

explanation.surface: Someone who is skilled at a craft puts it on show.
explanation.definitionFit: To boast a feature is to possess and show it off, as a hotel boasts a pool.

clue.text: English joiner mounting train

indicators.note: mounting in a down clue means the letters climb, so they are read from the bottom up

parts.note: a uniter is one who joins things

explanation.surface: An English carpenter climbs aboard a train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mounting' reverses the whole of E + UNITER, giving RETINUE.
explanation.definitionFit: A retinue is the group of attendants following an important person, as a train of followers does.

clue.text: Collapse after binge and cover the eyes

indicators.note: after places the word for collapse behind the word for binge

parts.note: a blind is British slang for a drinking spree
to fold is to collapse, as a business or a deckchair does

explanation.surface: Someone passes out after a drinking session and shields their eyes.
explanation.walkthrough: BLIND as a noun meaning a drunken binge is informal British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: A blindfold is a band tied over someone's sight; as a verb it means to mask them that way.

clue.text: As simple as Pooh said it might be

indicators.note: said shows the creature is spoken, not written

parts.note: Winnie-the-Pooh is a famous bear of children's books

explanation.surface: Something as plain as the bear of children's stories would put it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As' and 'it might be' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Bare means plain, unadorned, as in the bare facts.

clue.text: Getting pleasure from patience

definitions.meaning: gratifying one's own wishes and desires
tolerance or leniency shown towards someone

explanation.definitionFit: Indulgence is both self-gratification and forbearance, the lenient tolerance of another's faults.

clue.text: When the heat is on, good times for all boxers etc.?

definitions.text: good times for all boxers etc.?
definitions.meaning: boxers are a breed of dog, so a good time for all such animals

explanation.definitionFit: The hottest period of the year, named after the Dog Star, also reads literally as days for dogs.

clue.text: Exercise — or speaking grandly about it

definitions.text: Exercise — or speaking grandly about it

indicators.note: about says the grand speech goes around the word for exercise

parts.note: an oration is a formal, grandiloquent speech
PE is physical education, exercise at school

explanation.surface: A military drill, or a pompous speech on the subject of one.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines: 'it' points back to the exercise, so the grand speech is wrapped round it; 'or' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A military exercise or manoeuvre is an operation, a planned activity.

clue.text: Obsequiously wait as number of people hold up measure

indicators.note: in a down clue, holding up means supporting from below, so the crowd's number goes beneath the dance

parts.note: a measure is an old word for a stately dance
attendance is the number of people present

explanation.surface: Fawning staff wait while a crowd delays a new law.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to hover around someone, attending to their every whim in a servile manner.

clue.text: Put on thick coat but soaked

definitions.meaning: to apply plaster or any heavy layer over a surface

explanation.definitionFit: Plastering is laying on a heavy coat, and plastered is also slang for heavily drunk.

clue.text: Make pickings — slim, though good at first

indicators.note: at first puts the letter for good at the front of the word for slim

parts.note: lean means slim, without spare flesh

explanation.surface: Someone collects scraps, thin pickings though they start off well.
explanation.definitionFit: To glean is to gather leftover grain or scraps after the main harvest, picking up what remains.

clue.text: One is sensitive to what the pupil takes in

definitions.text: One is sensitive to what the pupil takes in

parts.words: One is sensitive to what the pupil takes in
parts.note: the pupil reads as a schoolchild learning lessons, but it is the opening of the eye, behind which sits the light-sensitive layer

explanation.surface: Someone attentive to what a student absorbs in class.
explanation.definitionFit: The light-sensitive tissue at the back of the eyeball receives the light admitted through the pupil.

clue.text: Split between bosom companions

parts.note: reads as a falling-out between close friends, but the bosom companions are a pair of breasts and the split is the gap between them

explanation.surface: Close friends fall out with each other.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a division or rift and the hollow between a woman's breasts.

clue.text: Personage in army occupying high rank

indicators.note: occupying puts the army inside the word for high rank, as troops occupy territory

parts.note: nobility is high social rank
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: An important figure in the army holds a senior post.
explanation.definitionFit: A notability is a prominent, important person, a celebrity or dignitary.

clue.text: Endeavour to introduce standards for signalling system

indicators.note: to introduce puts the detective's name in front of the word for standards

parts.note: Endeavour is the first name of Inspector Morse, the TV detective
a code is a set of standards or rules, as in a dress code

explanation.surface: An effort to bring in rules for a system of signals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endeavour' reads as a verb meaning try; it is the first name of Inspector Morse, the Oxford detective of British novels and TV.
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel Morse's dots-and-dashes alphabet is a method for sending messages by telegraph or light.

clue.text: Social occasion, rearranged as per notice

indicators.note: rearranged signals that the letters of per notice are reordered

explanation.surface: A party has been rescheduled in accordance with a notice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as' is a link word, not part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A reception is a formal party held to welcome guests or celebrate an event.

clue.text: Change dress

explanation.definitionFit: To shift is to move or alter, and a shift is also a plain loose frock.

clue.text: Say nothing in police stations

indicators.note: Say tells us the word for nothing is to be spoken out loud

parts.note: nix is slang for nothing

explanation.surface: Suspects keep silent in the custody suites.
explanation.walkthrough: A nick is British slang for a police station (and for a prison).
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a station house is a nick, so several are nicks.

clue.text: Copying device reproducing letters from clients

indicators.note: reproducing letters from means the letters of clients are reproduced in a new order

explanation.surface: A duplicating machine makes copies of customers' correspondence.
explanation.definitionFit: A stencil is a cut sheet through which ink is applied to reproduce a design or text.

clue.text: Varied inflections producing disasters when speaking

indicators.note: when speaking says the word for disasters is heard, not spelt

parts.note: accidents are mishaps or disasters

explanation.surface: Wavering voices result in catastrophes when someone talks.
explanation.definitionFit: Accidence is the part of grammar dealing with how words change form, their various endings.

clue.text: What is becoming one style of art's weird following

indicators.note: following puts the word for weird after the art style

parts.note: Art Deco is a style of design; its 's is a link
rum is British slang for odd or weird

explanation.surface: Something fashionable comes after a strange art movement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'becoming' means fitting or seemly, not turning into.
explanation.definitionFit: Decorum is proper, seemly behaviour, which is what is becoming in the sense of fitting.

clue.text: Such a bed isn't in this order

definitions.text: Such a bed isn't in this order

parts.words: Such a bed isn't in this order
parts.note: a prank bed with the sheet folded so the legs cannot go down is anything but neat, though the same phrase describes perfect tidiness

explanation.surface: A bed that is not tidily arranged.
explanation.walkthrough: Both phrases are British idioms: the prank bed made short-sheeted, and the expression for perfectly neat order.
explanation.definitionFit: The same compound names a short-sheeted joke bed and immaculate tidiness, so one is the opposite of the other.

clue.text: Long speech from North American embraced by son and daughter

indicators.note: embraced by puts the North American inside the letters for son and daughter

parts.note: the Cree are a Native North American people

explanation.surface: A lengthy address from a North American hugged by their children.
explanation.definitionFit: A screed is a long, often tedious piece of writing or speech, a lengthy harangue.

clue.text: Clubs circumscribed by censor's ruling

indicators.note: circumscribed by means surrounded, so the clubs letter sits inside

parts.note: to censor is to edit; the 's is a link
C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: Card games are restricted by the official's decree.
explanation.definitionFit: An edict is an official decree or order, a ruling issued by authority.

clue.text: Topless party-goer producing protest

indicators.note: Topless in a down clue means the top letter is cut off

parts.note: a raver is someone who goes to wild parties

explanation.surface: A half-naked reveller makes a complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: To aver is to assert or declare firmly, as to protest one's innocence.

clue.text: Like a bone among memorabilia church displayed

indicators.note: among says the letters sit inside the run of words memorabilia church

explanation.surface: A bone is shown alongside church keepsakes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'displayed' is a link word saying the letters are on show in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Iliac describes the ilium, the broad upper part of the pelvis, so it means relating to that bone.

clue.text: Overturning of popular interpretation

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable
a version is one person's interpretation or account

explanation.surface: A fashionable reading of something gets reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: Turning something upside down or back to front is an inversion of it.

clue.text: Warship blowing up enemy lair .

indicators.note: blowing up suggests the letters of enemy lair are exploded and reassembled

explanation.surface: A naval vessel destroys a hostile base.
explanation.definitionFit: A vessel built to lay explosive mines at sea is a kind of naval fighting ship.

clue.text: Run into small child in the joint at the corner

indicators.note: into tells us the letter for run goes inside the word for small child

parts.note: a mite is a tiny child
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Someone bumps into a toddler at the street corner.
explanation.definitionFit: A mitre is a woodworking joint where two pieces meet at an angle, typically forming a right-angled corner.
